scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Padua. Before Baptista's house.

lines.text: Is 't possible, friend Licio, that Mistress Bianca
lines.plainText: Is 't possible friend Licio that Mistress Bianca

lines.text: Doth fancy any other but Lucentio?
lines.plainText: Doth fancy any other but Lucentio

lines.text: I tell you, sir, she bears me fair in hand.
lines.plainText: I tell you sir she bears me fair in hand

lines.text: Sir, to satisfy you in what I have said,
lines.plainText: Sir to satisfy you in what I have said

lines.text: Stand by and mark the manner of his teaching.
lines.plainText: Stand by and mark the manner of his teaching

lines.text: Now, mistress, profit you in what you read?
lines.plainText: Now mistress profit you in what you read

lines.text: What, master, read you? First resolve me that.
lines.plainText: What master read you First resolve me that

lines.text: I read that I profess, The Art to Love.
lines.plainText: I read that I profess The Art to Love

lines.text: And may you prove, sir, master of your art!
lines.plainText: And may you prove sir master of your art

lines.text: While you, sweet dear, prove mistress of my heart.
lines.plainText: While you sweet dear prove mistress of my heart

lines.text: Quick proceeders, marry! Now tell me, I pray,
lines.plainText: Quick proceeders marry Now tell me I pray

lines.text: You that durst swear that your Mistress Bianca
lines.plainText: You that durst swear that your Mistress Bianca

lines.text: Lov'd none in the world so well as Lucentio.
lines.plainText: Lov'd none in the world so well as Lucentio

lines.text: O despiteful love! unconstant womankind!
lines.plainText: O despiteful love unconstant womankind

lines.text: I tell thee, Licio, this is wonderful.
lines.plainText: I tell thee Licio this is wonderful

lines.text: Mistake no more; I am not Licio.
lines.plainText: Mistake no more I am not Licio

lines.text: Nor a musician as I seem to be;
lines.plainText: Nor a musician as I seem to be

lines.text: But one that scorn to live in this disguise
lines.plainText: But one that scorn to live in this disguise

lines.text: For such a one as leaves a gentleman
lines.plainText: For such a one as leaves a gentleman

lines.text: And makes a god of such a cullion:
lines.plainText: And makes a god of such a cullion

lines.text: Know, sir, that I am call'd Hortensio.
lines.plainText: Know sir that I am call'd Hortensio

lines.text: Signior Hortensio, I have often heard
lines.plainText: Signior Hortensio I have often heard

lines.text: Of your entire affection to Bianca;
lines.plainText: Of your entire affection to Bianca

lines.text: And since mine eyes are witness of her lightness,
lines.plainText: And since mine eyes are witness of her lightness

lines.text: I will with you, if you be so contented,
lines.plainText: I will with you if you be so contented

lines.text: Forswear Bianca and her love for ever.
lines.plainText: Forswear Bianca and her love for ever

lines.text: See, how they kiss and court! Signior Lucentio,
lines.plainText: See how they kiss and court Signior Lucentio

lines.text: Here is my hand, and here I firmly vow
lines.plainText: Here is my hand and here I firmly vow

lines.text: Never to woo her more, but do forswear her,
lines.plainText: Never to woo her more but do forswear her

lines.text: As one unworthy all the former favours
lines.plainText: As one unworthy all the former favours

lines.text: That I have fondly flatter'd her withal.
lines.plainText: That I have fondly flatter'd her withal

lines.text: And here I take the like unfeigned oath,
lines.plainText: And here I take the like unfeigned oath

lines.text: Never to marry with her though she would entreat;
lines.plainText: Never to marry with her though she would entreat

lines.text: Fie on her! See how beastly she doth court him!
lines.plainText: Fie on her See how beastly she doth court him

lines.text: Would all the world but he had quite forsworn!
lines.plainText: Would all the world but he had quite forsworn

lines.text: For me, that I may surely keep mine oath,
lines.plainText: For me that I may surely keep mine oath

lines.text: I will be married to a wealthy widow
lines.plainText: I will be married to a wealthy widow

lines.text: Ere three days pass, which hath as long lov'd me
lines.plainText: Ere three days pass which hath as long lov'd me

lines.text: As I have lov'd this proud disdainful haggard.
lines.plainText: As I have lov'd this proud disdainful haggard

lines.text: And so farewell, Signior Lucentio.
lines.plainText: And so farewell Signior Lucentio

lines.text: Kindness in women, not their beauteous looks,
lines.plainText: Kindness in women not their beauteous looks

lines.text: Shall win my love; and so I take my leave,
lines.plainText: Shall win my love and so I take my leave

lines.text: In resolution as I swore before.
lines.plainText: In resolution as I swore before

lines.text: Mistress Bianca, bless you with such grace
lines.plainText: Mistress Bianca bless you with such grace

lines.text: As 'longeth to a lover's blessed case!
lines.plainText: As 'longeth to a lover's blessed case

lines.text: Nay, I have ta'en you napping, gentle love,
lines.plainText: Nay I have ta'en you napping gentle love

lines.text: And have forsworn you with Hortensio.
lines.plainText: And have forsworn you with Hortensio

lines.text: Tranio, you jest; but have you both forsworn me?
lines.plainText: Tranio you jest but have you both forsworn me

lines.text: Mistress, we have.
lines.plainText: Mistress we have

lines.text: Then we are rid of Licio.
lines.plainText: Then we are rid of Licio

lines.text: I' faith, he'll have a lusty widow now,
lines.plainText: I' faith he'll have a lusty widow now

lines.text: That shall be woo'd and wedded in a day.
lines.plainText: That shall be woo'd and wedded in a day

lines.text: God give him joy!
lines.plainText: God give him joy

lines.text: Ay, and he'll tame her.
lines.plainText: Ay and he'll tame her

lines.text: He says so, Tranio.
lines.plainText: He says so Tranio

lines.text: Faith, he is gone unto the taming-school.
lines.plainText: Faith he is gone unto the tamingschool

lines.text: The taming-school! What, is there such a place?
lines.plainText: The tamingschool What is there such a place

lines.text: Ay, mistress; and Petruchio is the master,
lines.plainText: Ay mistress and Petruchio is the master

lines.text: That teacheth tricks eleven and twenty long,
lines.plainText: That teacheth tricks eleven and twenty long

lines.text: To tame a shrew and charm her chattering tongue.
lines.plainText: To tame a shrew and charm her chattering tongue

lines.text: O master, master! I have watch'd so long
lines.plainText: O master master I have watch'd so long

lines.text: That I am dog-weary; but at last I spied
lines.plainText: That I am dogweary but at last I spied

lines.text: An ancient angel coming down the hill
lines.plainText: An ancient angel coming down the hill

lines.text: Will serve the turn.
lines.plainText: Will serve the turn

lines.text: What is he, Biondello?
lines.plainText: What is he Biondello

lines.text: Master, a mercatante or a pedant,
lines.plainText: Master a mercatante or a pedant

lines.text: I know not what; but formal in apparel,
lines.plainText: I know not what but formal in apparel

lines.text: In gait and countenance surely like a father.
lines.plainText: In gait and countenance surely like a father

lines.text: And what of him, Tranio?
lines.plainText: And what of him Tranio

lines.text: If he be credulous and trust my tale,
lines.plainText: If he be credulous and trust my tale

lines.text: I'll make him glad to seem Vincentio,
lines.plainText: I'll make him glad to seem Vincentio

lines.text: And give assurance to Baptista Minola,
lines.plainText: And give assurance to Baptista Minola

lines.text: As if he were the right Vincentio.
lines.plainText: As if he were the right Vincentio

lines.text: Take in your love, and then let me alone.
lines.plainText: Take in your love and then let me alone

lines.text: God save you, sir!
lines.plainText: God save you sir

lines.text: And you, sir! you are welcome.
lines.plainText: And you sir you are welcome

lines.text: Travel you far on, or are you at the farthest?
lines.plainText: Travel you far on or are you at the farthest

lines.text: Sir, at the farthest for a week or two;
lines.plainText: Sir at the farthest for a week or two

lines.text: But then up farther, and as far as Rome;
lines.plainText: But then up farther and as far as Rome

lines.text: And so to Tripoli, if God lend me life.
lines.plainText: And so to Tripoli if God lend me life

lines.text: What countryman, I pray?
lines.plainText: What countryman I pray

lines.text: Of Mantua.
lines.plainText: Of Mantua

lines.text: Of Mantua, sir? Marry, God forbid,
lines.plainText: Of Mantua sir Marry God forbid

lines.text: And come to Padua, careless of your life!
lines.plainText: And come to Padua careless of your life

lines.text: My life, sir! How, I pray? for that goes hard.
lines.plainText: My life sir How I pray for that goes hard

lines.text: 'Tis death for anyone in Mantua
lines.plainText: 'Tis death for anyone in Mantua

lines.text: To come to Padua. Know you not the cause?
lines.plainText: To come to Padua Know you not the cause

lines.text: Your ships are stay'd at Venice; and the Duke,—
lines.plainText: Your ships are stay'd at Venice and the Duke

lines.text: For private quarrel 'twixt your Duke and him,—
lines.plainText: For private quarrel 'twixt your Duke and him

lines.text: Hath publish'd and proclaim'd it openly.
lines.plainText: Hath publish'd and proclaim'd it openly

lines.text: 'Tis marvel, but that you are but newly come
lines.plainText: 'Tis marvel but that you are but newly come

lines.text: You might have heard it else proclaim'd about.
lines.plainText: You might have heard it else proclaim'd about

lines.text: Alas, sir! it is worse for me than so;
lines.plainText: Alas sir it is worse for me than so

lines.text: For I have bills for money by exchange
lines.plainText: For I have bills for money by exchange

lines.text: From Florence, and must here deliver them.
lines.plainText: From Florence and must here deliver them

lines.text: Well, sir, to do you courtesy,
lines.plainText: Well sir to do you courtesy

lines.text: This will I do, and this I will advise you:
lines.plainText: This will I do and this I will advise you

lines.text: First, tell me, have you ever been at Pisa?
lines.plainText: First tell me have you ever been at Pisa

lines.text: Ay, sir, in Pisa have I often been,
lines.plainText: Ay sir in Pisa have I often been

lines.text: Pisa renowned for grave citizens.
lines.plainText: Pisa renowned for grave citizens

lines.text: Among them know you one Vincentio?
lines.plainText: Among them know you one Vincentio

lines.text: I know him not, but I have heard of him,
lines.plainText: I know him not but I have heard of him

lines.text: A merchant of incomparable wealth.
lines.plainText: A merchant of incomparable wealth

lines.text: He is my father, sir; and, sooth to say,
lines.plainText: He is my father sir and sooth to say

lines.text: In countenance somewhat doth resemble you.
lines.plainText: In countenance somewhat doth resemble you

lines.text: [Aside.] As much as an apple doth an oyster, and all one.
lines.plainText: Aside As much as an apple doth an oyster and all one

lines.text: To save your life in this extremity,
lines.plainText: To save your life in this extremity

lines.text: This favour will I do you for his sake;
lines.plainText: This favour will I do you for his sake

lines.text: And think it not the worst of all your fortunes
lines.plainText: And think it not the worst of all your fortunes

lines.text: That you are like to Sir Vincentio.
lines.plainText: That you are like to Sir Vincentio

lines.text: His name and credit shall you undertake,
lines.plainText: His name and credit shall you undertake

lines.text: And in my house you shall be friendly lodg'd;
lines.plainText: And in my house you shall be friendly lodg'd

lines.text: Look that you take upon you as you should!
lines.plainText: Look that you take upon you as you should

lines.text: You understand me, sir; so shall you stay
lines.plainText: You understand me sir so shall you stay

lines.text: Till you have done your business in the city.
lines.plainText: Till you have done your business in the city

lines.text: If this be courtesy, sir, accept of it.
lines.plainText: If this be courtesy sir accept of it

lines.text: O, sir, I do; and will repute you ever
lines.plainText: O sir I do and will repute you ever

lines.text: The patron of my life and liberty.
lines.plainText: The patron of my life and liberty

lines.text: Then go with me to make the matter good.
lines.plainText: Then go with me to make the matter good

lines.text: This, by the way, I let you understand:
lines.plainText: This by the way I let you understand

lines.text: My father is here look'd for every day
lines.plainText: My father is here look'd for every day

lines.text: To pass assurance of a dower in marriage
lines.plainText: To pass assurance of a dower in marriage

lines.text: 'Twixt me and one Baptista's daughter here:
lines.plainText: 'Twixt me and one Baptista's daughter here

lines.text: In all these circumstances I'll instruct you.
lines.plainText: In all these circumstances I'll instruct you

lines.text: Go with me to clothe you as becomes you.
lines.plainText: Go with me to clothe you as becomes you
